questions.q: Which of these best matches this lesson's definition of data lineage?
options: The recorded path data takes from its origin, through every transformation, to where it's used
A backup copy of a database kept in a second data center
The total storage size a dataset occupies on disk
A list of every user who has ever logged into a system
questions.explain: Lineage is specifically about the path and the transformations along the way, not storage, backups, or access logs.

questions.q: In the package-tracking analogy, what does a single lineage 'hop' correspond to?
options: The entire delivery from start to finish
One scan event at one stage of the package's journey
The company that manufactured the package's contents
The customer who placed the original order
questions.explain: Just as a package is scanned at pickup, at a sorting facility, on a truck, and at delivery, a data hop is one recorded step — an extraction, a transformation, or a load.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what does the 'sharper' definition of lineage let you do that a plain definition misses?
options: Retrace exactly how a number got to be the number you're looking at, and see what else would be affected if a step changed
Automatically fix incorrect data without human review
Permanently delete outdated records
Compress a dataset to save storage space
questions.explain: The plain 'tracking where data comes from' definition misses the transformations in between; the sharper version includes retracing every step and understanding downstream impact.

questions.q: Which of these is given as an everyday example of lineage-like tracing in this lesson?
options: A bank wire transfer's trail showing where funds were sent, cleared, and deposited
The total number of employees at a bank
A password stored in a password manager
The color scheme of a mobile banking app
questions.explain: A wire transfer's trail — sent from one account, cleared through an intermediary, deposited to another — is lineage for money, the same concept applied to data.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why does Data Lineage & Impact Analysis build directly on Metadata Management & Business Glossary?
options: Because you can't usefully trace where a column's value came from unless you can already name and locate that column via the dictionary and catalog
Because the two courses cover entirely unrelated topics
Because this course replaces the need for a business glossary
Because lineage only applies to software that has no metadata at all
questions.explain: The prior course built the vocabulary and inventory (names, definitions, catalog locations); lineage is the next layer, tracing movement on top of that identity.
